name: Mickie Hennig
fact: The 1987 Talisman gives her full name as Kathryn Michelle Hennig and files her as a junior, so she was in the class of 1988. The Juniors divider page of that volume carries a pull quote signed "Mickie Hennig" about the middle of a degree: the newness had worn off, graduation was close, and she was still unsure what she wanted. Her single index entry, 316, is that page.

name: Drew DeLozier
fact: A Louisville junior, and chairman of Associated Student Government's Rules and Elections Committee in the spring of 1988. He announced the finalists of the presidential primary that Scott Whitehouse and Todd Ragland led, and it was DeLozier who ruled that Cambron's proposed write-in campaign was not legal, a ruling Rules and Elections, the Judicial Council, dean of student life Howard Bailey and vice president for student affairs Jerry Wilder all upheld.

name: Bill Parsons
fact: A Bowling Green junior in 1988-89. The Talisman photographed him in warpaint at Midnight Mania, the midnight opening practice of the 1988-89 men's basketball season in Diddle Arena on Friday 14 October 1988, which drew about 2,000 fans.

name: Heather Falmlen
fact: By 1991-92 she was Associated Student Government president and student regent, and a Winchester senior. That autumn ASG investigated a rumour that she had received a diamond bracelet from Board of Regents chairman Joe Iracane as a bribe, ahead of the board's vote for a new chairman on 31 October; officers feared it would sway her vote. Falmlen denied receiving a bracelet, and Iracane kept the chairmanship when nobody else was nominated.

name: Brandon T. Rucker
fact: A sophomore from Bedford living in Poland Hall in 1993-94, the year before he was treasurer.

name: Jamie Fite
fact: She won the secretary's race against Darlene Lodmell, 452 votes to 396 with 34 no votes, in the spring 1997 Associated Student Government election. The same results box gives Keith Coffman 534 over Carlene Lodmell 334 for president, Leigh Ann Sears 498 over David Apple 371, and Chad Lewis 515 over Steve Roadcap 327.

src.label: College Heights Herald, 24 April 1997, p. 3, election results box

name: Steve Roadcap
fact: A Louisville sophomore who chaired the campus improvements committee. He introduced the resolution to install two lanes on the track and repair it, telling the Senate the track had not been repaired since 1968 and that cross country and track coach Curtiss Long was losing revenue over it; he also carried a lighting resolution for the McCormack fifteen-minute lot, the DUC south lawn walkway to Tate Page Hall and the Wetherby faculty and staff lot, and organised the SGA campus clean-up of 18 October. He lost the spring 1997 race to Chad Lewis, 327 to 515.

src.label: College Heights Herald, 1996-97 session reports and the 24 April 1997 results box

name: Ricky Jordan
fact: A Hyden freshman in his second semester of SGA membership when he stood in the March 2005 election. He sat on the academic affairs and legislative research committees and was SGA archivist, co-chair of student affairs and director for the Outlet Alliance. He ran on making faculty evaluations available to students, saying the student body had a right to assess professors, and on graduation contracts, calling it absurd with rising tuition that students should not get out in four years. The 2007 Senate minutes give his full name as Ricky Skylar Jordan.

src.label: College Heights Herald, SGA election special, 15 March 2005, p. 4C

name: R. Skylar Jordan
fact: He ran for administrative vice president in the spring 2008 election while serving as chief of staff, on a slate of independents with Johnathon Boles for president and Kayla Shelton for executive vice president, against the Red Towel Party. He campaigned against higher education budget cuts, arguing students could not be expected to carry them, and opposed the plus/minus grading system that had first been proposed in autumn 2003.

name: Cain Alvey
fact: A sophomore special education major from Lewisport. As administrative vice president he managed an SGA budget of over $124,000 and administered Organizational Aid, was a resident assistant in McCormick Hall, and represented the student body in the University Senate. Standing for president in spring 2013 he proposed a Design-a-Course option, a need-based book scholarship fund, an expanded winter and summer session scholarship carried over from the Dodds administration, graduate and professional test preparation programmes, and an expansion of the Safe Ride and Purple Line late-night bus service he had begun exploring as AVP.

src.label: WKU SGA, Spring 2013 Election: The Candidates, p. 1

name: Brad Cockrel
fact: Originally from Texas, he went to Ottawa Township High School in Illinois and then Illinois Valley Community College, where he was student treasurer and student trustee of the college's student government and vice president of leadership for Phi Theta Kappa. He spent seven months teaching conversational English in the Czech Republic. At WKU he was a double major in mechanical engineering and philosophy with a mathematics minor. Standing for executive vice president in spring 2013 he ran on shared interest groups for freshmen, more tutoring in the higher sciences and mathematics, better conditions for student workers and easier cardboard recycling.
